items.claim: Rewritten 'no stack' test no longer reaches the no-stack branch
items.consequence: The test named 'creates new stack if original error has no stack' now passes a real `new Error('original')`, which always carries a string `stack` in Node, so the guard `if (originalError && originalError.stack)` at src/error/GraphQLError.js:195 is truthy and the constructor copies the original stack instead of taking the captureStackTrace fallback. The only assertion, `expect(e.stack).to.be.a('string')`, is satisfied by the copied stack, so the test is now a weaker duplicate of 'uses the stack of an original error' and would stay green if the `&& originalError.stack` fallback were broken or removed. Verified by running the constructor with both fixtures: post-diff `e.stack === original.stack` is true; the pre-diff `{ message: 'original' }` fixture produced a fresh stack. Restoring a stackless original (cast to `any`) and asserting the stack differs makes the test cover the branch its name claims.
items.proposed_fix: Keep a stackless original while satisfying Flow, e.g. `const original: any = { message: 'original' };` (the pre-diff fixture; `any` is accepted because .flowconfig has no [strict] lint section, as locatedError-test.js already relies on), or `const original = new Error('original'); (original: any).stack = undefined;`. Then strengthen the assertion to `expect(e.stack).to.be.a('string').and.not.equal(original.stack)` so the captureStackTrace fallback is distinguished from the copy-the-original-stack path.

native_payload.intent: Enable Flow strict type checking on the error-module tests (GraphQLError, locatedError, printError) and the jsutils inspect test by replacing @noflow with @flow strict and rewriting fixtures so they type-check (invariant-narrowed AST nodes, a shared dedent-ed Source, `any` casts, one $FlowFixMe). Also widen the public `declare class GraphQLError` constructor's `nodes` parameter to accept `null`. Runtime behavior must be unchanged and the rewritten tests must still exercise the behaviors they did before.

residual_risks: src/error/GraphQLError.js:25 vs :94 -- the public `declare class` constructor now admits `null` for `nodes`, but the implementation function's own annotation (`nodes?: $ReadOnlyArray<ASTNode> | ASTNode | void`) was not widened. Runtime is correct today (`Array.isArray(null)` is false and `null ? [nodes] : undefined` yields undefined; verified by scratch run), but Flow checks the constructor body only against the narrower implementation type, so a future body change that distinguishes `undefined` from `null` would pass Flow while crashing for the `null` callers the public declaration now admits. Consider widening line 94 to match line 25. (raised by: adversarial; corroborated by correctness)
